body.statement: Along the legal path \(\theta_{\gamma}\), \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta_{\gamma})=\{\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{1,4\}\}\) and \(h(\theta_{\gamma})=(\{1\},\{1,2,3,4\})\) for \(\gamma\ne0\), whereas at \(\gamma=0\) all six two-element target sets are compatible and \(h(\theta_0)=(\varnothing,\{1,2,3,4\})\).  For equal environment sample sizes, there exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c\sqrt n|\gamma|\le\delta_n(\theta_{\gamma})\le C\sqrt n|\gamma|\) for all sufficiently small nonzero \(\gamma\).
body.justification: The witness proves that profile collision changes compulsory labels and that the abstract information distance has a concrete first-order scale.
body.gap: Bacchiocchi et al. study rotation sets at repeated HSVAR eigenvalues, but not a legal acyclic SCM path whose complete labeled target family changes with a computed Gaussian-information rate.
body.consumer: The example is an early kill test for implementations of augmentation, classification, and pivot memoization in the smallest nontrivial case.
